name: Equally likely outcomes → count
description: When outcomes are genuinely uniform, probability is a counting problem. First always ask: are these outcomes actually equally likely?

name: Complement is easier than direct counting
description: 'At least one' is the tell: compute P(none) and subtract from 1.

name: Condition on the first/last event
description: Sequential processes where later outcomes depend on earlier ones: condition on the first (or last, or pivotal) event and use total probability.

name: Bayes / reverse conditioning
description: You are told a LATER or DOWNSTREAM outcome and asked about an earlier or upstream one. Direction reversal is the tell for Bayes.

name: Symmetry and exchangeability
description: When positions, players, or draws are interchangeable, exploit it: many hard-looking probabilities collapse to simple ratios.

name: Indicator variables + linearity of expectation
description: When only E[X] is needed, write X as a sum of indicators. Linearity needs NO independence — that is the whole point.

name: Recursive expectation / first-step analysis
description: Repeating or self-similar processes: define a state, condition on the first step, and solve the resulting equations.

name: Memoryless property
description: Geometric/exponential settings where the past does not matter: restarting the clock simplifies the computation.

name: Order statistics
description: Max/min/k-th of several draws: work with P(max ≤ x) or the tail-sum formula E[X] = Σ P(X ≥ k).

name: Inclusion–exclusion
description: Overlapping 'bad events' that complement counting alone cannot untangle: add, subtract pairwise, add triples…

name: Work backward
description: When the end state is more constrained than the start, reason from the end.

name: Invariant / conservation argument
description: Find a quantity the process never changes; it often decides the answer immediately.

name: Martingales & optional stopping
description: Fair-game structure: construct a martingale and apply optional stopping to get expectations of hitting times/probabilities.

name: Market-making & betting intuition
description: Quote two-sided markets around fair value; width reflects uncertainty and adverse selection; update on flow.

name: Fermi estimation
description: Decompose an unknown quantity into factors you can bound within ~3x; errors cancel in the product.

name: Mental math
description: Fast, accurate arithmetic under pressure: round-and-correct, factor tricks, difference of squares.

name: Pigeonhole / extremal reasoning
description: Guarantee-type questions ('must there exist…'): pigeonhole and extremal principles beat case analysis.
